title: Conformance cases
description: The conformance suite's cases, each defined once and grouped by area, the invariants every case checks, and the spec's anchors no case covers. A case's ID and the fields that say what it expects of whom, what it reaches and relies on, and where it applies, and an invariant's ID, expectation and needs, are frozen with the protocol version, as protocol/README.md's Freezing says.

areas.description: The areas, each by its name, which starts the ID of every case it holds. The guide site's case list groups the cases by area, in this order.

invariants.description: The checks the runner applies in every case beside its own expectation, once the components each needs are built, each by its ID. A violation fails the case it happened in, naming the invariant. An invariant isn't a case, so no expected failure names one.

uncovered.description: Each anchor of the spec that no case or invariant covers, by its citation, with why none can. The guide site's build fails on an anchor that is neither covered nor listed here, and on one listed here that a case covers.

name.description: An area's name, in lowercase kebab-case.

case_id.description: A case's ID: its area's name, a period, then its own name in lowercase kebab-case, such as endpoint.invalid-refused. Kebab-case keeps an ID from reading as a contract name, which keeps its file's spelling.

invariant_id.description: An invariant's ID: invariant, a period, then its name in lowercase kebab-case.

component_id.description: The ID of a component in components.yaml.

text.description: Plain text, in sentences. Text between backticks renders as code.

citation.description: An anchor of the spec a case covers: the document, protocol-v<n> for a protocol version's spec or connector-api for the connector API's reference, then # and the anchor. An anchor without a period is a heading's, as the site slugs it. An anchor with one is a table row's, named as the contract's files name it: a registry entry as <section>.<name>, such as rejections.invalid_session; a header as headers.<name>; a reserved route as routes.<operationId>; or a connector API entry as <section>.<name>, such as errors.unsupported_transport. A citation names no page, so a document's pages can move without changing it.

transport.description: A transport, as the connector API names it: unix for a Unix domain socket (POSIX), npipe for a named pipe (Windows) and tcp for loopback TCP (every platform).

via.description: What a request goes through, as the adapter protocol names it: the connector's untyped request, or the Backend's primitive.

platform.description: A family of operating systems, as the spec's endpoint URLs name them.

backend.description: What a case talks to. app: a backend serving the reference app on the case's transport, which in a connector run and in a server case is pipeapi's server, and in the baseline run the app under plain uvicorn on loopback. fake: the runner's fake server, which stands in for a backend. On loopback, either listens on a fixed port, with no rendezvous file, unless the case names a generated endpoint or the rendezvous file.

area.description: An area of the case list.

title.description: The area's heading on the site.

description.description: One sentence on what the area's cases cover.

cases.description: The area's cases, each by its ID, which starts with the area's name.

case.description: One case. Its ID, its expectation, its kind, what it reaches and relies on (its backends, needs and relies_on) and where it applies (its transports, platforms, vias and once) are frozen once its protocol version is released; changed behavior is a new case.

title.description: A short title, a sentence without its period.

expectation.description: What the case sets up and what must hold, checkably: a check waits for an observation, never for a set time, unless the rule is about a fixed duration passing, which the expectation names; an absence, such as no further hello or no event, is checked once the case observes a control that would have shown the event by then, which the expectation names, such as the result of the call that would have caused it, a request sent afterwards, or a second Backend whose own outage came later; durations are lower bounds, and an upper bound is wide and says so.

kind.description: server: run once against pipeapi's server, driven by the runner's raw client. connector: run once for each connector, through its adapter.

backends.description: What the case talks to, which sets the components it needs beyond its own needs: with app, pipeapi's server and its listener on the case's transport, except in the baseline run; with fake, the fake server. Empty, it reaches nothing, such as a case that checks a refusal before any connection.

needs.description: The components the case needs beyond those its backends and the run imply: the server, the listeners, the fake server, the baseline adapter and the reference app are never listed. The runner skips the case while one isn't built.

transports.description: The transports the case applies to. Unset, every transport its platform has: unix and tcp on POSIX, npipe and tcp on Windows.

platforms.description: The platforms the case applies to. Unset, both.

vias.description: What its requests go through, the case running once for each, as it does for each transport. Unset, it doesn't vary by them, and sends its requests through the untyped request.

once.description: Whether the case runs once on each platform, on one transport it applies to, since its result doesn't depend on the transport. Unset, it runs on each transport.

relies_on.description: The optional capabilities of an adapter, as the adapter protocol names them, that the case needs. The runner skips the case, as not applicable, for a connector whose adapter's hello doesn't declare them.

baseline.description: Whether the baseline adapter runs the case too, against the reference app under plain uvicorn on loopback: its checks hold of any HTTP client and server that serve the app.

slow.description: Whether the case lasts 15 seconds or more by design, since a fixed duration must pass, such as one of the protocol's durations, so the runner gives it longer to finish.

covers.description: The anchors of the spec whose rules the case checks. A case whose rule no page states yet covers none, and names in its expectation, as #<n>, the issue whose design it follows.

invariant.description: A check the runner applies in every case, once the components it needs are built.

title.description: A short title, a sentence without its period.

expectation.description: What holds in every case, frozen as a case's expectation is.

needs.description: The components the invariant's check needs, such as the server for a check of what the server does, frozen as a case's needs are. The runner skips the invariant while one isn't built, and fails a run where each is built but the runner has no check for it.

covers.description: The anchors of the spec whose rules the invariant checks.
